desc:
In one move you may delete either the first or the last element of nums, and you subtract the deleted value from x. Return the smallest number of moves that makes x exactly 0, or -1 if that cannot be done.

The array changes after every move, so later moves operate on what remains.

nums = [1, 1, 4, 2, 3], x = 5
remove 3 (right), then 2 (right): 5 - 3 - 2 = 0
result = 2
hints: Whatever you remove is some prefix plus some suffix of the array. What is left over?
The remaining middle part is a contiguous subarray whose sum equals sum(nums) - x. Fewest removals means longest middle.
All values are positive, so a variable-size sliding window can find the longest subarray with a given sum. Return n - longest, or -1 if no such subarray exists.
editorial: Removing elements from both ends leaves a contiguous block in the middle. If the removed values sum to x, the block sums to target = total - x. Minimising the moves is the same as maximising the block length.

If target < 0 the answer is -1. If target == 0 everything must be removed, so the answer is n. Otherwise, because all numbers are positive, a window sum grows when extended right and shrinks when the left edge moves, so a two-pointer sweep finds the longest subarray summing to target in O(n). The result is n - longest, or -1 if none was found.
